text: G52 written in notes-D3.md under G51's readings, before any A20 line was read or ruled. It sets out A20's words and counts; reads P01 as D3a-02 read it (a call to place posted in the room's threads, a visitor's or a kindred group's call included, since A20's mechanism names calls that flood the host sub) and P20 by G26 and its readings; and gives six readings from the arrow's words: the first end (VC marks a visitor's first call); the second end; one act (RM marks a removal notice whose only record of the call is the post it removes); the flood in words (MW where the first line answers canvas posts, NF where it answers none: the falsifier's second clause, recorded present); the close (AC marks a first line after hour 73 that follows a call made while the canvas ran); and the bound. It also gives the absent rule, the instantiate classes (O-A, O-H; BOUND, J, NC, NL, ONE, AFTER), the restrict rule under G9, the census plan and the draws. d3_a20_g52_quote_check.py (new): 6 quoted segments, all found in A20's record. Next: the packets

A slip: a command sent in parallel with the G52 note was a placeholder, a shell variable whose name begins 'for_' and a no-op. It ran with no output and changed nothing. The same slip happened twice at D3a-46. Its cause is sending a second call where no second command was needed. From here, a turn holds a second call only when that call does real work.

G52 amendment 1 written in notes-D3.md (D3a-47, 20 October 2026, before any A20 line was ruled; it applies to every A20 line). G52's instantiate paragraph let one post whose words name the call or the flood first, and the line after, show the order. A flood is not a call, and an objection to the flood needs canvas posts (the bound's partly constitutive clause). So a post's words show the order only where they name calls posted in the room first, and the line after. A line that names only canvas posts, threads or spam shows the line alone, and its first end must come from a coded call in its concepts or in the coded posts above them in their chain. G52's readings 1 to 7, stated while reading A20's instantiate window i447_000 (25 lines), before its rows are written; none an amendment. (1) Under amendment 1, lines whose concepts name only the flood, with no coded call in the line or its chains, show one end (anarchism-049; austria-046; bardmains-064; belgium-054, whose c0125 is a design wish; berserk-052; brasil-050; buffalobills-047; chibears-046; cubers-056: ONE). ONE covers one end or neither. (2) A proposal to make or show a work is the starter's (R01, A02's first end), not a call (FinalFantasy c0035, a question whether to show the banner). A removal notice that calls the removed post an idea or a proposal records no call, so RM is kept for removals whose words show the removed post as a call (armenia-027 c0094: ONE; babymetal c0101, c0102). (3) A warning that the work is changed or attacked, or a call to keep an eye out, is P01's hold form, as G51 read the first end (argentina c0507; babymetal c0117; chicubs c0163). A warning that the work will soon be attacked, with no ask, is not a call (borussiadortmund c0084, by a writer who also posts in r/thenetherlands). Where the line's first line comes before its first call, the line shows the bound's pattern: argentina-050 asks to use one post at h+32.69, then c0507 at h+67.40; babymetal-049 removes a proposal and names a dedicated thread at h+26.52, then c0117 at h+44.01; chicubs-043 asks to ban canvas talk in the game thread at h+58.71, then c0163 at h+58.97 (BOUND). (4) A submission that reports the chosen design, invites members into the chat and walks them through running the placement script is a call to place, answered in part by machine (D3a-02's calls answered by machine). A reply in its chain asking to consolidate the posts follows it (bitcoin-047 c0357 to c0361, then c0365: O-A, R, MW). (5) A call, then a reply in its chain asking to put the posts in one place, to ban or remove them, or objecting to the spam, shows the order in the thread (AMD-047 c0214 then c0215; OnePiece-042 c0246 then c0248; buffalo-044 c0016 then c0023; canada-043 c0482 then c0484; chicago-050 c0076 then c0077, a call that addresses the room and asks help for another group, so marked VC; crusaderkings-058 c0002 then c0013, a canvas sub to leave the messy comment section, as C2 sampled it: O-A, MW). A call, then a megathread, a hub ruling or a canvas sub in another thread, shows the order by the hours (FinalFantasy-044 c0037, h+56.56, above c0071, then c0038, h+56.82: O-H, R; borussiadortmund-041 c0089, h+49.66, then c0088, h+51.94; colombia-023 c0001, h+17.60, then c0025, h+37.94: O-H, MW). (6) A call made after hour 73 is not this arrow's first end (croatia-059 c0210, h+73.10: AFTER). (7) A coordination channel opened to bring order to scattered threads, with no line stated that spares the sub, is T4-010's ground, not P20 (G26's reading of chats), so the line shows neither end (2007scape-047 c1199: ONE). Coded posts above the lines quoted into d3_cites_A20_i1.txt. Window i447_000 classed: O-A 7 (1 VC), O-H 3, BOUND 3, ONE 11, AFTER 1. Next: A20-inst-spec-1.txt

G52's readings 8 to 12, stated while reading A20's instantiate window i447_025 (25 lines), before its rows are written; none an amendment. (8) A request to change the room's work and a call to remake a figure are calls. Where a megathread rule or a moderator's limit on canvas posts comes first, the line shows the bound's pattern (czech-046 c0255, h+68.84, then c0268, h+71.07; fireemblem-052 c0227, h+36.62, then c0229, h+36.94: BOUND). (9) A petition that names the logo and its place on the canvas asks members to make it, so it is a call, unlike a question whether to make a work (reading 2), and a request in its chain for a megathread follows it (flyers-034 c0201, h+54.16, above c0203, h+54.35: O-A, R, MW). A call for help to save the work, above a sticky that answers repeated threads, shows the order (japan-042 c0025, h+24.41, above c0063, h+45.44: O-A, R, MW). (10) A call to write a taunt on another room's flag is a call to place, as D3a-02 read calls aimed at another work, and a reply objecting to the spam follows it (england-044 c0014 then c0015). So do dbz-065 c0074 then c0075 and floridagators-034 c0118 then the sticky reply c0119 (O-A, MW). A call, then a megathread or an official coordination thread in another thread, shows the order by the hours (donaldglover-059 c0020, h+25.19, then c0079, h+49.74; hellointernet-044 c0001, h+3.10, then c0068, h+46.83: O-H, MW). (11) A call shown only after the close, for a later canvas, is not the first end, so a line whose megathread talk comes before the close and whose only call comes after it is AFTER (denmark-066 c0254, h+63.39, and c0262, h+71.91, then c0339, h+88.17). (12) A sticky that answers the disarray of many threads is P20's megathread whatever its motive (G26's reading of stickies), and with no call the line shows one end (dota2-051 c1021: ONE). One end also shows in danganronpa-047, de-056 (a moderator's reply whose parent is not coded), earthbound-063, eesti-038, factorio-043, fivenightsatfreddys-050, france-051, frankocean-047, funhaus-050, gorillaz-049, greece-049 (a removal whose notice does not show the removed post as a call), homestuck-051, ireland-042 and italy-034 (ONE). G52's readings 13 to 17, stated while reading A20's instantiate window i447_050 (25 lines), before its rows are written; none an amendment. (13) These are not calls: a post that presents the work or reports its progress (korea c0095; nin c0104, an update by another room's writer); a design question about what to overlap (malaysia c0124); and a warning to builders not to cover a border (monsterhunter c0152). They are P03's, P02's and P04's. A question why the room is not on the canvas is a proposal, as reading 2 reads it (lego c0127; onepunchman c0056: ONE). (14) An exhortation to make a flag at a named spot, to expand the work into empty space, to keep the art up, to move and rebuild, or to build another flag is a call (lebanon c0207; monero c0085; monsterhunter c0154; nyjets c0105; pakistan c0135). Where a moderator's removal rule or a request to crack down comes first, the line shows the bound's pattern (lebanon-049 c0114 and c0116, h+44.82, then c0207, h+47.85; monero-057 c0060, h+39.37, then c0085, h+46.79; monsterhunter-045 c0132, h+52.89, then c0154, h+53.74: BOUND). (15) A call, then a reply in its chain that routes the talk, objects or names the spam, shows the order in the thread (marvel-031 c0044 then c0045; minecraft-062 c0226 then c0227; nintendo-063 c0131 then c0132, a visitor's request for help, so VC; nyjets-048 c0105 above c0106, R; pakistan-070 c0135 above c0136, R: O-A, MW). A call above a later removal, with the first line in another thread at a later hour, shows the order by the hours (malaysia-050 c0136, h+64.80, above c0146, then c0129, h+66.14: O-H, R, MW). (16) A request for one thread so that members can coordinate one plan, with no word of the sub's business, is coordination (P04), not P20, as G26 read chats. So the first line in msu-043 is the moderator's removal, after the close, of other rooms' requests, whose words name the requests first: the order in the post's words, marked VC and AC (c0032, h+76.55: O-H, MW). (17) math-034 is NONPORTABLE. Its plan post is answered in reply by an objection whose words name such posts as already removed, so its concepts show the order, and it is a particular marked PO (c0057, h+48.16, then c0058, h+48.53).
